findings.summary: ALSA is a Linux kernel software framework and API for sound card device drivers, designed to automatically configure hardware and manage multiple audio devices. It provides a user-space library that abstracts hardware capabilities through software plugins, enabling standardized application access to features like volume control and sample rate conversion. ALSA superseded the older Open Sound System and supports hardware MIDI synthesis, full-duplex operation, and multiprocessor-friendly drivers. It organizes sound cards numbered 0-7 with interfaces for PCM, control, timer, raw MIDI, and sequencer, represented as device files in /dev/snd. The architecture includes kernel drivers and a shared user-space library (alsa-lib) that presents standardized abstractions across diverse hardware.

mechanisms.title: Kernel device drivers and core framework
mechanisms.explanation: ALSA operates as part of the Linux kernel, including core framework and device drivers for physical sound cards. These drivers handle hardware-specific control and data transfer for up to eight sound cards, each addressable by ID, and expose interfaces such as PCM, control, timer, raw MIDI, and sequencer via device files in /dev/snd.

mechanisms.title: User-space alsa-lib with software plugins
mechanisms.explanation: A user-space shared library provides API abstractions for applications and implements plugins that transform or adapt audio streams. Plugins such as "softvol" provide software emulations of hardware controls (e.g., volume) when underlying hardware lacks them, and "dmix" enables software mixing and sample rate conversion. This layer presents a standardized interface across disparate hardware, allowing applications to remain agnostic of specific device capabilities.
